title: All-Inclusive in Novigrad, Croatia 2027: Options & Prices
metaDescription: Novigrad in Istria has no confirmed all-inclusive hotel. Nearest options in Funtana, Poreč and Umag, with price ranges against half-board and apartments.
content:
## Does Novigrad Have All-Inclusive Hotels?

No. Novigrad (Cittanova) is a small walled town on Istria's west coast, and its accommodation is mainly boutique hotels, guesthouses, campsites with holiday homes and private apartments. Current listings show no resort in the town that sells a true all-inclusive plan, so no Novigrad property is named here as all-inclusive.

The main hotels are Hotel Nautica on the marina (rooms from about €113 a night), Hotel Cittar, Blu Mare, Aminess Vival Maestral and the adults-only Palazzo Rainis. They are built around breakfast or half-board, and the town's restaurants and konobas make up the rest. A search for "all-inclusive Novigrad" mostly returns resorts in nearby towns, because booking sites group the whole area under the Novigrad name.

## Nearest All-Inclusive Hotels to Novigrad

All-inclusive on this stretch of coast is concentrated in three resort areas, each a 15–25 minute drive away:

- **Funtana (about 20 km south):** Maistra Select Funtana All Inclusive Resort is the best-known option. It is rated around 9.1/10 by more than 2,000 guests and sits close to Vrsar harbour.
- **Poreč, Plava and Zelena Laguna (about 16 km south):** Hotel Zorna Plava Laguna is a beachfront 3-star with a pool, and Hotel Laguna Albatros sits about 100 m from a beach in Zelena Laguna. Both are listed with all-inclusive meal plans.
- **Umag (about 17 km north):** Hotel Sol Aurora All Inclusive, Katoro 18, is a 4-star with 306 rooms, about 300 m from Katoro beach.

All-inclusive offers change from year to year. Confirm the meal plan, drinks hours and children's rules on the hotel's own booking page before paying.

## What All-Inclusive Usually Covers Here

Istrian all-inclusive packages follow a fairly standard pattern:

- Breakfast, lunch and dinner as buffet or semi-buffet
- Local house wine, beer, soft drinks and water with meals, often also at the bar during set hours
- Afternoon snacks, ice cream or pool-bar items
- Pool access, sun loungers and kids' club or animation in higher categories

Typical exclusions are premium spirits, coffee specialities outside meal hours, à la carte restaurants, spa treatments, excursions and the tourist tax. The tourist tax is a few euros per adult per night. Check the bar hours, because some hotels end drinks service at 22:00 or 23:00.

## Price Per Person Per Night: All-Inclusive vs Half-Board vs Apartment

These are rough planning ranges for adults sharing a double room. Real rates move with the date, room type and how early you book.

| Type | Peak (mid-July to late August) | Shoulder (May–June, September) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive (Funtana, Poreč, Umag) | €90–150 | €55–90 |
| Half-board hotel (incl. Novigrad hotels where offered) | €70–110 | €45–70 |
| Private apartment, room only | €25–55 | €18–35 |

An apartment's food costs are on top of that. Groceries and a mix of cooking and eating out typically add €25–45 per person per day in Istria. A restaurant main course in Novigrad runs about €14–25. For a couple, an apartment with partial self-catering usually ends up 30–45% below all-inclusive in peak season. In shoulder season the gap narrows to 15–30%, because all-inclusive rates fall faster than apartment rates.

Children change the maths. Most resorts give free or heavily discounted places to children under 6–7 in a parents' room, which makes all-inclusive much better value for families than the adult rates suggest.

## Who All-Inclusive Suits

- **Families with children under 8:** Meals are available at fixed times without any planning, snacks and drinks are covered, and a pool and kids' programme sit on site. Child discounts make this the strongest case.
- **Short stays of 3–5 nights:** Shopping, cooking and cleaning are not worth the effort on a long weekend.
- **Guests who stay on site:** The plan pays off if you use the pool, beach and bar every day.
- **Groups with fussy eaters:** A buffet covers different tastes without arguments over a restaurant choice.

## Who Is Better Off Self-Catering

- **Stays of 7 nights or more:** An apartment with a kitchen costs less and avoids buffet fatigue by day five.
- **Couples and adults without children:** There is no child discount to offset the high adult rate.
- **Food-focused travellers:** Istria is known for truffles, fresh fish, olive oil, Malvazija wine and local oysters from the nearby Lim and Mirna areas. Buffet food rarely matches a good konoba.
- **Day-trippers:** If you plan to visit Poreč, Rovinj, Motovun or Piran, you will miss many paid-for meals.

The all-inclusive wristband and the Novigrad old town do not work well together. Staying in Funtana or Umag and driving to Novigrad for dinner means paying for a buffet you skip. Choose one approach per trip, and for Novigrad itself, choose the apartment.

## Local Tips for Novigrad

- **Book apartments early.** The best-rated ones in town and on the Mirna side fill by spring for August.
- **Check the beach.** Novigrad's Mandrač and Rivarela areas have pebble and concrete bathing platforms. Sandy-feeling beaches for small children are limited, so check this before you commit to the town.
- **Mix plans.** A family can book half-board in Novigrad for 3 nights and self-catering for the rest.
- **Ask about drinks hours** and whether the plan covers beach-bar drinks, not only meal-time drinks.
- **Shoulder season** (late May, June and September) gives the best value: sea temperatures are about 20–24 °C, rates are lower and restaurants are less crowded.

## Conclusion

Novigrad is a half-board and self-catering town. Families with small children who want all-inclusive should stay in Funtana, Poreč or Umag, and visit Novigrad as a day trip. Everyone else gets better value, and better food, from an apartment in Novigrad itself.

faq.question: Is there an all-inclusive hotel in Novigrad, Croatia?
faq.answer: No all-inclusive hotel or resort in Novigrad itself is confirmed by current listings. Hotels in town sell bed-and-breakfast or half-board. The nearest all-inclusive hotels are in Funtana, Poreč and Umag.

faq.question: Where is the nearest all-inclusive resort to Novigrad?
faq.answer: Poreč's Laguna area is closest, about 16 km away, with beachfront hotels such as Hotel Zorna Plava Laguna. Umag (Hotel Sol Aurora All Inclusive) is about 17 km north, and Maistra Select Funtana All Inclusive Resort is about 20 km south.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost per person per night near Novigrad?
faq.answer: Expect roughly €90–150 per adult in peak season and €55–90 in shoulder season. Half-board is about €20–40 cheaper per person, and an apartment is cheaper again before food costs.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive worth it for families in Istria?
faq.answer: Yes, for families with children under 8, because child discounts are large and meals and snacks are predictable. It is less worthwhile for adults only, or for stays longer than a week.

faq.question: What is usually included in all-inclusive in this part of Croatia?
faq.answer: Three meals a day, house drinks at set hours, snacks, and pool and loungers. Premium drinks, à la carte restaurants, spa and excursions usually cost extra, as does the tourist tax.

faq.question: When is the cheapest time for an all-inclusive stay near Novigrad?
faq.answer: Late May, June and September are cheapest. Rates can be 30–40% below mid-July and August levels, while the sea is still warm enough for swimming.
